File Number: 22993T1
SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE
TYPE | Rezoning Attachment
3948-54 N. Elston Avenue
From Cl-1 to C1-3

The Property

The Subject Property is improved with an existing mixed-use building containing ground-floor
commercial space and seven residential units above. The Subject Property is located at 3948-54
N. Elston Avenue Chicago, IL 60618 (PIN: 13-23-107-007-0000; 13-23-10-008-0000) (henceforth
referred to as the “Subject Property”), and is located in the C1-1 Neighborhood Commercial
Zoning District. The surrounding area is comprised of varying zoning districts, including B3-1,
RS-3, and Cl-!.

The Project

The Applicant, Thirty Four Holdings LLC, is the owner of the Subject Property and seeks a map
amendment to change the zoning from a Cl-! to a C1-3 Neighborhood Commercial Zoning
District. The Applicant has owned the property since 2021. When the property was transferred
there were seven occupied units. The property’s smallest unit is +/- 550 sq ft and the largest unit
is 1250 square feet. Under Chicago Zoning Ordinance Sec. 17-3-0402, buildings inaCl-1 Zoning
District must provide at least 2,500 square feet of lot area per dwelling units. The proposed map
amendment would reduce the requirement to 400 square feet per unit, bringing the building’s
current occupancy into compliance with zoning regulations. The Applicant does not intend to
perform any structural work to alter floor plans or increase unit density. The goal is to maintain
the building in its existing condition, consistent with how it has been since the Applicant purchased

the property.

The Applicant is filing a Type | rezoning application and seeks all relief necessary, as allowed by
the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, for the attached plans, including two Administrative Adjustments,
pursuant to 17-13-1003-EE and 17-13-1003-GG, to reduce the required automobile parking from
15 spaces to 14 spaces (a one-space reduction) and to reduce the bicycle parking from seven to
zero spaces due to physical space constraints. Section 17-10-0207-C requires one space for every
dwelling unit. For the commercial space on the first floor, Section 17-10-0207-O requires 1.66
spaces for every 1,000 square feet. The building has about 5,197 square feet which would require
eight spaces for the commercial unit and seven for each residential unit. In total, the code requires
parking for 15 spaces, while the property currently provides 14. The Applicant requests an
administrative adjustment through Section 17-13-1003-EE as the building is within 1,320 feet of
a CTA Bus Line and is not in a Zoned D district. Because the property is approximately 295 feet
from the nearest bus stop at Irving Park Road and Central Park Avenue, the zoning code permits
the Applicant to reduce required parking spaces to zero. However, given the existing 14-space

parking lot, the Applicant will only require a one-space reduction to preserve the building’s current
character, Pursuant to 17-10-0102-B(2), residential buildings within 1320 feet of a CTA bus line

corridor must contain at least one bicycle parking space per dwelling unit. CDOT requires that
bicycle racks may only be installed on sidewalks with a minimum width of ten feet. The sidewalk

in front of the Subject Property is five feet wide, rendering installation impossible. Due to this
physical impossibility, the Applicant requests an additional administrative adjustment pursuant to

Section 17-13-1003-GG.

administrative adjustment:
